review_notes: I read the whole target file (lines 1–90). I also read its definition site (BUShortPhaseDecay.lean), BUShortAbsorptionShifted.lean, BUShortCoreLower.lean and BUShortWeightedComparison.lean. I looked for other files with the same shifted-weight conversion and found none beyond these. The only repeat I found worth reporting is the conversion between buShortShiftedWeight and exp(-(2*a*buShortB scale)) * buShortCarlemanWeight. The block is short, so the case rests on its recurrence: three integral copies in two files, plus two integrability copies. I did not check that the proposed lemma compiles. It would sit right after the buShortShiftedWeight definition in BUShortPhaseDecay.lean, and I did not confirm that MeasureTheory names are in scope there. I assumed the lemma can be written with qualified names or an added `open`.

findings.problem: The tail of the proof pulls the constant exp(-(2*a*buShortB scale)) out of an integral against buShortShiftedWeight. It does this by unfolding the weight, using integral_const_mul, then congr, funext and ring. The same five-line argument appears twice more in BUShortAbsorptionShifted.lean, in bu_short_integral_shift_le (the hleft and hright blocks). Two further proofs, in BUShortCoreLower.lean and BUShortWeightedComparison.lean, repeat the integrability counterpart (hbase.const_mul (Real.exp (-(2 * a * buShortB scale))), then convert, funext, dsimp [buShortShiftedWeight], ring). The relation between the shifted and Carleman weights is therefore re-derived at each use. The target also carries a long `change` statement and a `let c := Real.exp ...` only to set up this rewrite.
findings.proposed_change:
Add a lemma next to the definition of buShortShiftedWeight in BUShortPhaseDecay.lean:

theorem integral_buShortShiftedWeight_mul (scale a : ℝ) (K : Set ParabolicPoint) (F : ParabolicPoint → ℝ) :
    (∫ z in K, buShortShiftedWeight scale a z * F z ∂(volume : Measure ParabolicPoint)) =
      Real.exp (-(2 * a * buShortB scale)) * ∫ z in K, buShortCarlemanWeight a z * F z ∂(volume : Measure ParabolicPoint)

Proof sketch: `rw [← MeasureTheory.integral_const_mul]; congr 1; funext z; simp only [buShortShiftedWeight]; ring` (the pointwise step is mul_assoc). An optional companion would turn Integrable/IntegrableOn of the Carleman-weighted integrand into the shifted-weighted one. It would use Integrable.const_mul and the same pointwise identity.

Use in the target: after `apply hscaled'.congr'; filter_upwards [] with ε; symm`, the `change` and the whole `rw … ring` tail reduce to `exact integral_buShortShiftedWeight_mul scale a _ _`. The `let c` can then be inlined.

Use in bu_short_integral_shift_le: replace hleft and hright by `rw [integral_buShortShiftedWeight_mul, integral_buShortShiftedWeight_mul]` and keep the existing `nlinarith only [h']` step.

The companion lemma would likewise shorten hFE in BUShortCoreLower.lean and hleft in BUShortWeightedComparison.lean.
findings.benefit: The relation between the shifted and Carleman weights is proved once, next to the definition, and each use becomes a single rewrite. The proofs no longer mention exp(-(2*a*buShortB scale)) or unfold buShortShiftedWeight. Any later change to the weight definition needs only one repair. The target's proof shrinks to its mathematical content: the limit from the unshifted case, scaled by a constant.
